args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy as v2.3.1-rc in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Next steps: confirm health and error rate recover on v2.3.0, find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and look into why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

**Rollback:**
- **The problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Target version:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rolling back to it didn't need approval, since it has been healthy in production before.
- **Result:** All three regions now run v2.3.0. The service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.

**Incident INC-0001:** It describes the failure, the rollback to v2.3.0 and the recovery afterwards. Follow-ups listed in it:
- Keep watching the service on v2.3.0.
- Find out why v2.3.1 fails.
- Find out why it reached production even though its staging build (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy.
